questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist faces a medical emergency at 2 a.m. The only prescription on hand is marked 'no substitution', the prescribed brand is not in stock, and an interchangeable product on the Massachusetts list is. The pharmacist dispenses the interchangeable product. Which statements about this dispensing are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A medical emergency permits filling a 'no substitution' prescription this way when the brand is out of stock.
The pharmacist's own note of the emergency completes what the regulation asks of the pharmacy.
The date, hour and nature of the emergency must be recorded on the prescription or in the pharmacy system.
The purchaser must indicate acceptance of the deviation in writing.
The deviation runs only toward the cheaper product, never toward the brand as written.

questions.stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to set up her medications in a reusable weekly planner. She brings in a sealed, in-date bottle of her lisinopril that a pharmacy across town dispensed last month, and asks that it go in alongside the medications this pharmacy supplies. The pharmacy has a designated preparation space and written planner procedures. What should the pharmacist do about the lisinopril?

choices.text: Include it, since the patient requested the planner service and the bottle is sealed and in date.
Decline to place it in the planner, because it was dispensed by a different pharmacy.
Include it after transferring the original prescription to this pharmacy on the spot.
Include it once the patient signs an acknowledgement that she supplied the product.
Include it, provided the planner is labelled to show which pharmacy supplied each drug.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy prepares multi-drug single-dose compliance packages. For one patient the prescriber asks that a moisture-sensitive tablet be included; the FDA-approved labeling directs that the product be kept in its original container with the desiccant until use. The pharmacy has a designated space, full written procedures for this packaging type, and a compatible package component. What controls whether the tablet may be included?

choices.text: The prescriber's request, since compliance packaging is prepared on the prescriber's direction.
The pharmacy's written procedures, since the regulation asks for procedures rather than outcomes.
The patient's informed acceptance of any reduction in shelf life.
The FDA-approved labeling, which the packaging must not contradict.
The Board's Schedule II and III maintenance-medication policy.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is commissioning an automated system that counts tablets, fills vials and applies labels. To keep cells full, the pharmacy plans to top up a cell without emptying it first, so two manufacturer lot numbers will sit together. Which statements about this arrangement are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Comingling lot numbers in one cell is prohibited outright.
The pharmacy must hold a policy to quarantine all comingled lots if a single lot is recalled.
A pharmacist's visual check of the finished vial satisfies the verification requirement.
Controlled substance accountability need not be addressed until the system handles Schedule II drugs.
The system must use a technological verification such as bar code, weight or RFID checking.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy proposes to place an automated dispensing device holding controlled substances in the staff room of a group medical practice that is not a licensed health care facility. Every removal would be logged, the cabinet would be alarmed, and the pharmacy would maintain full written procedures. What is the correct assessment?

choices.text: The arrangement fails, because the device must be located in a licensed health care facility.
The arrangement works, because the pharmacy's procedures cover accountability and security.
The arrangement works if the practice registers the cabinet with the Board separately.
The arrangement works for Schedule III through V, and fails only for Schedule II.
The arrangement fails, because a pharmacy may not use an automated dispensing device for controlled substances at all.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is fitting out a new prescription area. It proposes a dorm-style refrigerator with a small freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space for the few frozen products it stocks, with a continuous temperature logger fitted. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy may not use an appliance with a freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space.
A freezer unit must be frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle unless the Board approves otherwise.
A continuous logger showing in-range temperatures makes the appliance acceptable.
The pharmacy's procedures must include a response protocol for any out-of-range temperature.
A combination refrigerator/freezer unit would not be permitted either.

questions.stem: A patient telephones a Massachusetts pharmacy and asks it to bring over a prescription held at another pharmacy. The receiving pharmacy tells her it will charge a small administrative fee for the work, and that she must telephone the other pharmacy herself to start the process. Which statement best describes the receiving pharmacy's position?

choices.text: Both the fee and the requirement that she call the other pharmacy are permissible.
The fee is permissible, but the pharmacy must make the call itself.
The fee is not permissible, and the pharmacy may act as her agent to obtain the transfer.
The fee is not permissible, but the patient must still initiate the transfer herself.
Neither is permissible, because only the transferring pharmacy may charge or initiate.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts community pharmacy dispenses a Schedule II opioid for a patient who lives in a long-term care facility, delivered to the facility for her use there. A technician asks whether the state consumer educational pamphlet on narcotic drugs must go out with it. What is the correct answer?

choices.text: Yes, because the pamphlet duty attaches to every Schedule II narcotic dispensing.
Yes, unless the facility confirms in writing that it will counsel the resident itself.
No, because delivery to a facility is not a dispensing to a consumer.
No, because the pamphlet is required only for a first fill of a given opioid.
No, because the patient is a resident of a long-term care facility.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy licensed for sterile compounding prepares two products on the same morning: a sterile infusion for an outpatient, and a sterile preparation for a patient admitted as an inpatient in the same hospital under its institutional licence. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both containers must be labelled as a sterile compounded preparation.
The outpatient container must also carry the pharmacist-contact telephone number.
The telephone must be staffed during regular hours of operation and at least 56 hours a week.
The inpatient preparation must also carry the telephone number, since the pharmacy does sterile compounding.
The pharmacist reachable on that number must have access to the patient's records.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is dispensing a Schedule II opioid prescribed for a 15-year-old patient. The patient's mother is collecting the medication. The pharmacist has already explained the potential adverse risks of the opioid. What does the statute require next?

choices.text: Nothing further, because a minor cannot be dispensed an opioid antagonist.
Offer to dispense an opioid antagonist to the mother as the minor's parent.
Offer to dispense an opioid antagonist only if the prescriber has also ordered one.
Obtain the prescriber's authorisation before raising an opioid antagonist with the family.
Record that the patient is a minor and treat the antagonist offer as inapplicable.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts patient presents a Schedule II oxycodone prescription written by her Massachusetts physician nine days earlier. She asks the pharmacy to dispense only part of it today and to hold the balance. A colleague says the initial partial fill is already too late because it is past the fifth day after the issue date. Which assessment is correct?

choices.text: The colleague is right; the five-day limit runs from the issue date for any Schedule II partial fill.
The colleague is right, but only because the drug is a narcotic rather than a stimulant.
The colleague is wrong; the five-day limit reaches only prescriptions filled on the out-of-state pathways.
The colleague is wrong; no deadline governs a patient-requested partial fill of a Schedule II prescription.
The colleague is wrong; the five-day limit runs from the first dispensing rather than from the issue date.

questions.stem: A prescriber telephones a pharmacy about a drug for which FDA requires a Medication Guide. She has concluded that receiving the Guide would not be in this particular patient's best interest, and directs that it not be provided. At the counter the patient asks the pharmacist for written information about the medicine. What must the pharmacist do?

choices.text: Provide the Medication Guide, because the patient has requested information.
Withhold the Guide but supply the manufacturer's patient information leaflet instead.
Withhold the Guide, because the prescriber's clinical direction controls at the counter.
Withhold the Guide unless the patient puts the request in writing.
Contact the prescriber for permission before providing anything in writing.

questions.stem: A neighbour collects a prescription on behalf of a housebound patient. The product is one for which FDA requires a Medication Guide. The pharmacy's practice is to hold the Guide on file and give it to the patient at the next visit, on the view that the Guide belongs to the patient personally. What is the correct assessment of that practice?

choices.text: It is sound, because a Medication Guide must be provided directly to the patient.
It is sound, provided the pharmacy telephones the patient to summarise the Guide.
It is sound only where the collecting person is not a family member.
It is unsound, because the Guide goes to the patient or the patient's agent at the time of dispensing.
It is unsound, because the Guide must be posted to the patient within 24 hours of dispensing.

questions.stem: A customer at a Massachusetts pharmacy counter asks to buy 5 grams of pseudoephedrine base today. He mentions that he bought 5 grams elsewhere eleven days ago. Which statements about the federal quantity limits are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A regulated seller may sell him up to 7.5 grams in a single calendar day.
The pharmacy is the party federally restricted to 3.6 grams per purchaser per day.
Today's sale would exceed the 3.6 gram daily seller restriction.
Buying a further 5 grams within the 30-day window would put the purchaser over the 9 gram limit.
The 9 gram limit applies to sellers rather than to purchasers.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts hospital pharmacy dispenses oxycodone twice for the same patient on the same day: once against a medication order while she is an inpatient on the ward, and once against a discharge prescription she takes home that afternoon. Which dispensings must be reported to the Prescription Monitoring Program?

choices.text: Neither, because both were dispensed by a hospital pharmacy.
Both, because the reporting duty reaches every Schedule II dispensing.
The inpatient medication order only.
Both, unless the hospital reports inpatient administration through a separate system.
The discharge prescription only.

questions.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist reads a journal piece arguing that a particular Schedule VI medicine is being diverted and should be watched. Her pharmacy does not report its dispensing to the Prescription Monitoring Program. What determines whether that dispensing becomes reportable?

choices.text: The pharmacy's own assessment that the drug carries a bona fide potential for abuse.
Rescheduling of the drug out of Schedule VI into Schedules II through V.
A prescriber's request that the pharmacy report its dispensing of the drug.
A determination by the Commissioner, followed by notification to dispensers.
Publication of the diversion evidence in the professional literature.
